# 3 Marketing Tasks You Can Hand to AI This Week

> **In short:** AI tools like ChatGPT can take over three time-sucking marketing jobs — fixing lead funnel drop-offs, drafting campaign copy, and writing reports — so you spend more time on the work only you can do.

If you've ever stared at a marketing dashboard at 6pm wondering where the day went, you're not alone. Most marketing teams spend more time producing assets and reports than they do thinking about customers — and that's exactly where AI can step in. You don't need to overhaul your whole workflow. You just need to find the three jobs that drain you, and let AI do the first draft.

## 1. Find where your funnel leaks (and what to say next)

A "funnel" (the path a person takes from first hearing about you to buying) leaks at every stage. People sign up for your free trial, browse a few pages, then disappear. AI can't fix your product — but it can spot the pattern in your data and write the message that brings them back.

Export a list of users who stopped engaging after a key moment (say, day 3). Paste the column headers and a sample of 10–20 rows into ChatGPT, then try:

💬 *"Look at these users who dropped off after day 3. What patterns do you see in their last action? Suggest 3 short re-engagement email subject lines and opening lines for each pattern."*

You'll get a draft you can edit. The win isn't the email — it's that the AI looked at 20 rows in 10 seconds, when it would have taken you an hour.

## 2. Build campaign assets without starting from a blank page

Every campaign needs the same handful of things: a headline, three social posts, an email body, maybe a short ad. AI drafts these in seconds. You edit them in minutes.

Try a prompt like this:

💬 *"You're a marketer for [your product]. Write 5 LinkedIn post variations announcing our [campaign name] in a friendly, conversational tone. Keep each under 150 words. End with a soft call to action."*

Then ask for a shorter version, a punchier version, a version that opens with a question. The point isn't that the AI is brilliant on the first try — it's that you never face a blank page.

## 3. Turn a messy data table into a one-page report

Reporting is the marketing job almost everyone dreads. AI is genuinely good at this: paste a table, ask for a summary, get paragraphs you can drop straight into a slide.

Try this:

💬 *"Here is last month's campaign performance data [paste table]. Write a 5-sentence summary for our leadership team. Highlight the top performer, the biggest miss, and one thing to test next month. Use plain language — no jargon."*

You'll know it worked when the AI gives you back something that sounds like a report, not a data dump.

## What this means for you

- **If you run a small business or solo project**: You don't need a marketing team to look like one. Use AI to draft the assets, then edit them in your own voice. The biggest risk isn't AI sounding like AI — it's you never publishing because the blank page won.
- **If you work on a marketing team**: Pick the one task your team hates most (usually reporting or follow-up emails) and pilot AI on that first. Don't try to change everything at once.
- **If you don't work in marketing but collaborate with one**: Understand that the people writing your campaign copy are probably juggling 12 other things. A small nudge like *"I drafted an outline with AI — can you polish it?"* goes further than *"can you just whip something up?"*

## Wrap-up

AI won't replace the marketer who understands the customer — but it can replace the hour they spend formatting a report. Pick one of the three tasks above, try it this week, and notice how much time lands back in your day. The next step is small: open ChatGPT (a free account works for all three prompts), paste one real table from your own work, and ask for a 5-sentence summary. That's the whole experiment.
